::: {.callout-note}
## Setup

These exercises use the development versions of `mixtime` and `ggtime`, so the code can't be run in this page. Run it in RStudio, after loading this setup code:

```r
library(fpp3)
library(mixtime) # Load last

# Use mixtime for the time index of each dataset
tourism <- tourism |>
  mutate(Quarter = yearquarter(Quarter))
aus_production <- aus_production |>
  mutate(Quarter = yearquarter(Quarter))
PBS <- PBS |>
  mutate(Month = yearmonth(Month))
aus_retail <- aus_retail |>
  mutate(Month = yearmonth(Month))
vic_elec <- vic_elec |>
  mutate(Time = mixtime(Time))
pedestrian <- pedestrian |>
  mutate(Date_Time = mixtime(Date_Time))
```
:::

## Exercise 2

::: {.callout-caution}
## Exercise 2

Identify the `index` and `key` variables of the `aus_accommodation` dataset.

Then use `as_tsibble()` to convert it into a tsibble.
:::

```r
library(fpp3)
read.csv(
  "https://workshop.nectric.com.au/wombat2026/data/aus_accommodation.csv"
)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solution

The `index` is `Date` and the `key` is `State`. `Date` is read as text, so parse it first.

```r
accommodation <- read.csv(
  "https://workshop.nectric.com.au/wombat2026/data/aus_accommodation.csv"
)
accommodation |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(Date = as.Date(Date)) |>
  as_tsibble(index = Date, key = State)
```
:::

## Exercise 3

::: {.callout-caution}
## Exercise 3

Redo the previous exercise, but this time use the appropriate time class for the index variable.

You should see the frequency of the tsibble matches the quarterly frequency of the measurements.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Hint

Parse the text with `date()`, then use `yearquarter()`.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solution

```r
accommodation |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(Date = yearquarter(date(Date))) |>
  as_tsibble(index = Date, key = State)
```
:::

## Exercise 4

::: {.callout-caution}
## Exercise 4

Try calculating the total tourists visiting Victoria from the `tourism` dataset.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Hint

Use `filter()` to keep only visitors to "Victoria", then `summarise()` to calculate the total trips.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solution

```r

  filter(State == "Victoria") |>
  summarise(Total_Trips = sum(Trips))
```

## Exercise 5


::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solution

```r
vic_tourism <- tourism |>
  filter(State == "Victoria") |>
  summarise(Trips = sum(Trips))
vic_tourism |>
  autoplot(Trips)
```

There is a strong seasonal pattern (peaking in Q1 and lowest in Q2 and Q3), a slight trend, and no clear cycles.

## Exercise 6

::: {.callout-caution}
## Exercise 6

Decompose the cost of antidiabetic scripts, then plot its components and the seasonally adjusted series.
:::

```r
a10 <- PBS |>
  filter(ATC2 == "A10") |>
  summarise(Cost = sum(Cost) / 1e6)
a10_dcmp <- a10 |>
  model(STL(???)) |>
  components()

# Plot the components
a10_dcmp |> ???

# Plot the seasonally adjusted data
as_tsibble(a10_dcmp) |> autoplot(???)
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Hint

Are the patterns additive or multiplicative?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solution

```r
a10 <- PBS |>
  filter(ATC2 == "A10") |>
  summarise(Cost = sum(Cost) / 1e6)
a10_dcmp <- a10 |>
  model(STL(log(Cost))) |>
  components()

# Plot the components
a10_dcmp |> autoplot()

# Plot the seasonally adjusted data
as_tsibble(a10_dcmp) |>
  autoplot(exp(season_adjust)) +
  labs(y = "Cost ($ millions)")
```

`log()` makes the patterns additive, and `exp()` returns the seasonally adjusted series to dollars.
:::

## Exercise 7

::: {.callout-caution}
## Exercise 7

Find and plot the three most seasonal series.

*Extension: which series have the strongest trend?*
:::

```r
tourism |>
  features(???, ???) |>
  slice_max(???, n = 3) |>
  inner_join(x = tourism, y = _,
    by = join_by(Region, State, Purpose)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = ???, y = ???)) +
  geom_time_line() +
  facet_grid(vars(Region, State, Purpose),
    scales = "free_y")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solution

```r
tourism |>
  features(Trips, feat_stl) |>
  slice_max(seasonal_strength_year, n = 3) |>
  inner_join(x = tourism, y = _,
    by = join_by(Region, State, Purpose)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Quarter, y = Trips)) +
  geom_time_line() +
  facet_grid(vars(Region, State, Purpose),
    scales = "free_y")
```

For the extension, use `trend_strength` in `slice_max()`.
:::

# Seasonality and calendars

## Exercise 8

::: {.callout-caution}
## Exercise 8

Loop the time axis of this plot with `coord_loop()`.
:::

```r
pbs_scripts <- PBS |>
  summarise(Scripts = sum(Scripts))
pbs_scripts |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Month, y = Scripts)) +
  geom_time_line() +
  coord_loop(time_loops = ???)
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Hint

`time_loops` is a mixtime duration, such as `weeks(2L)` for a fortnight.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solution

```r
pbs_scripts |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Month, y = Scripts)) +
  geom_time_line() +
  coord_loop(time_loops = years(1L))
```
:::

## Exercise 9

::: {.callout-caution}
## Exercise 9

Describe the shape of the seasonal pattern.

When are the most scripts (the peak) and the least scripts (the trough) issued?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solution

Scripts peak in December and are lowest in February. Check the shape with a season plot:

```r
pbs_scripts |>
  gg_season(Scripts, period = years(1L))
```
:::

## Exercise 10

::: {.callout-caution}
## Exercise 10

Plot the shape of the seasonal pattern, in which quarter does Australia produce the most and least gas?
:::

```r
aus_production |>
  autoplot(Gas)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solution

```r
aus_production |>

```

Peak production is in Q3, with a trough in Q1. Seasonality is getting stronger recently.
:::

## Exercise 11

::: {.callout-caution}
## Exercise 11

Is the seasonal pattern in the total subsidised prescriptions (`Scripts`) in Australia changing over time?
:::

```r
pbs_scripts <- PBS |>
  summarise(Scripts = sum(Scripts))
pbs_scripts |>
  autoplot(Scripts)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solution

```r
pbs_scripts |>
  model(STL(Scripts)) |>
  components() |>
  gg_subseries(season_year, period = years(1L))
```

The number of scripts in December is dropping rapidly. They appear to be redistributed into Oct, Nov, and Jan.
:::

## Exercise 12

::: {.callout-caution}
## Exercise 12

Use `date()` with `index_by()` to aggregate to daily data, then use `gg_season()` to plot the weekly seasonal pattern.
:::

```r
pedestrian |>
  filter(Sensor == "Southern Cross Station") |>
  index_by(???) |>
  summarise(Count = sum(Count)) |>
  gg_season(???)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solution

```r
pedestrian |>
  filter(Sensor == "Southern Cross Station") |>
  index_by(Day = date(Date_Time)) |>
  summarise(Count = sum(Count)) |>
  gg_season(Count, period = weeks(1L))
```
:::

## Exercise 13

::: {.callout-caution}
## Exercise 13

Create a calendar plot for the first few months of pedestrians at Southern Cross Station.

Can you see any holiday effects?
:::

```r
pedestrian |>
  filter(Sensor == "Southern Cross Station") |>
  filter(yearmonth(Date_Time) <= yearmonth(???)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = ???, y = ???)) +
  geom_time_line() +
  coord_???(rows = ???, cols = ???)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solution

```r
pedestrian |>
  filter(Sensor == "Southern Cross Station") |>
  filter(yearmonth(Date_Time) <= yearmonth("2015 Apr")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Date_Time, y = Count)) +
  geom_time_line() +
  coord_calendar(rows = weeks(1L), cols = months(2L)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Time", y = "Pedestrian count")
```

Holidays (such as Easter and Anzac Day) have much lower counts.
:::

## Exercise 14

::: {.callout-caution}
## Exercise 14

Use an STL decomposition and `gg_season()` to clearly show the seasonal patterns in pedestrian traffic.
:::

```r
ped_dcmp <- pedestrian |>
  filter(Sensor == "Southern Cross Station") |>
  fill_gaps(Count = 0) |>
  model(STL(Count)) |>
  components()
ped_dcmp |>
  autoplot()
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solution

```r
ped_dcmp |>
  gg_season(season_year, period = years(1L))
ped_dcmp |>
  gg_season(season_week, period = weeks(1L))
```

The weekly seasonal pattern interacts with the daily seasonal pattern, so the model doesn't work here. STL is additive, so interactions between different seasonalities are not captured.
:::

## Exercise 15

::: {.callout-caution}
## Exercise 15

Use features to find an interesting series in `tourism` (e.g. strongly seasonal, or an unusual peak).

Plot its seasonality, then explain what you see. Is the pattern changing over time?
:::

```r
tourism |>
  features(Trips, feat_stl) |>
  filter(
    seasonal_strength_year > ???,
    format(seasonal_peak_year) == ???
  )

tourism |>
  filter(Region == ???, Purpose == ???) |>
  gg_season(Trips, period = ???)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solution

```r
# Which strongly seasonal series peak in Q2?
tourism |>
  features(Trips, feat_stl) |>
  filter(
    seasonal_strength_year > 0.6,
    format(seasonal_peak_year) == "Q2"
  ) |>
  select(Region, Purpose, seasonal_peak_year)

tourism |>
  filter(Region == "Blue Mountains") |>
  filter(Purpose == "Holiday") |>
  model(STL(Trips)) |>
  components() |>
  gg_subseries(season_year, period = years(1L))
```

The Q2 peak (autumn, Easter?) is growing since 2010. Q4 is weakening, and is now the trough.
:::
